metadata.content: Harrison Armstrong's distance covered stats highlight Everton midfielder's impact under David Moyes this season | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Harrison Armstrong's distance covered stats highlight Everton midfielder's impact under David Moyes this season In this exclusive interview with David Moyes, the Everton manager discusses the development of Harrison Armstrong since being recalled from a loan spell at Preston North End and the reasons why he believes the 19-year-old midfielder can still improve... Adam Bate Football Features Writer @ghostgoal Monday 23 November 2026 10:07, UK Image: Harrison Armstrong has massive potential and David Moyes believes he can become a top-notch midfield player Harrison Armstrong has started every Premier League game for Everton this season, ranking in the top three for distance covered in the competition going into the weekend. This has been some year for a player who started 2026 on loan at Preston North End. There was talk of a big move to Nottingham Forest in the summer and interest from elsewhere remains as Everton try to persuade him to sign a new contract. Supporters will be desperate for one of their own to stay. And David Moyes feel the same way. "He is a big player for us," the Everton manager tells Sky Sports . "For a 19-year-old young midfield player he is doing really well. I hope he can continue to do that." That recall from Preston in January already feels like a pivotal moment in Armstrong's career

messages.text: 'This cannot continue' - Ferrari to hold fresh Leclerc-Hamilton talks after collision

metadata.summary: Ferrari team boss Frederic Vasseur says he will hold further discussions with drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton after their latest tangle in the Las Vegas Grand Prix, admitting such incidents "cannot continue".
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc clashes 'cannot continue' after Las Vegas GP with Frederic Vasseur to speak to drivers again | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc clashes 'cannot continue' after Las Vegas GP with Frederic Vasseur to speak to drivers again Ferrari's drivers involved in costly on-track incident for second time in three races, with Leclerc given penalty in Vegas; Frederic Vasseur bemoans a "lack of respect"; watch every session of the Qatar GP live on Sky Sports F1 from Friday, with Sunday's race at 4pm Sunday 22 November 2026 17:03, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari team-mates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc react after they crashed into one another at the Las Vegas Grand Prix Ferrari team boss Frederic Vasseur says he will hold further discussions with drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton after their latest tangle in the Las Vegas Grand Prix, admitting such incidents "cannot continue". After costly clashes in Monza and Mexico City earlier this season, the Ferrari drivers came together when battling over sixth place with 12 laps to go on the Strip circuit in a race dominated by slip-streaming in which the leading runners were covered by a handful of seconds for most of the race. Leclerc attempted to overtake Hamilton with a move down the inside of Turn Seven but made contact with the Briton, who was spun around. Stewards found Leclerc at fault and handed him a 10-second penalty

messages.text: Jamaica level series with dominant win over England

metadata.summary: England failed to extend their lead in the Vitality Netball Horizon Series with Jamaica, as the visitors claimed a dominant 55-40 win at the Copper Box Arena.
metadata.content: England 40-55 Jamaica: Vitality Roses beaten in London as Sunshine Girls impress and level four-Test Horizon Series | Netball News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England 40-55 Jamaica: Vitality Roses beaten in London as Sunshine Girls impress and level four-Test Horizon Series Jamaica bounced back from losing their opening match to level the four-Test series against the Vitality Roses; England will travel to Jamaica to play further matches on December 5 and 6, as preparation continues for next year's Netball World Cup Sunday 22 November 2026 21:52, UK Image: Jamaica levelled the four-Test series with a 55-40 victory England failed to extend their lead in the Vitality Netball Horizon Series with Jamaica, as the visitors claimed a dominant 55-40 win at the Copper Box Arena. A day on from a dramatic 47-46 victory in the series opener at the same London venue, England were second-best as the Sunshine Girls claimed a comfortable victory and levelled the four-Test series. The visitors scored six consecutive points on their way to opening a 15-7 advantage after the first quarter, then the Commonwealth Games silver medallists extended their lead to 11 points by half-time.
